task.description: Extend test coverage for the §2.2 delta added since your original test file was written. The security-critical property added in this rework is the one-way gate: Letflow.Identity.sync_role_claims_from_token/3 seeds group_members from JWT claims ONLY when a user's role_claims_synced_at is nil, and must NEVER re-fire once set -- meaning a revoked-then-still-claiming user's access must NOT silently resurrect on a later login/token refresh. Your original test file (test/letflow/plugs/iss0736_oidc_live_revocation_test.exs) proves the live-check-on-next-request property but was written against a fixture that pre-seeded group_members directly, sidestepping the sync path entirely. Add a NEW test (in the same file or a new one under test/letflow/) that: (1) simulates a first-ever OIDC login for a brand-new user whose JWT claims a real recognized role (e.g. PROCESS_OPERATOR) with NO pre-existing group_members row -- assert the sync fires, group_members gets a row, role_claims_synced_at gets stamped, and the request succeeds with that role; (2) simulates the tenant_admin revoking that role (Identity.remove_group_member/3) -- assert immediate 403 on retry with the same JWT (same property as the original test, now via the real sync path); (3) simulates that SAME user hitting the pipeline AGAIN with the SAME (still role-claiming) JWT after revocation -- assert the sync does NOT re-fire (role_claims_synced_at unchanged, no new group_members row, still 403) -- this is the critical regression-proof for the one-way gate. Run all new tests and quote real pass output. Run everything in the foreground -- no background Monitor waiting.
acceptance_criteria: New test proves the sync-on-first-login path (not just pre-seeded fixtures)
New test proves the one-way gate specifically: sync does not re-fire after revocation even though the JWT still claims the role
Real quoted test output showing all pass
No product code changed -- test files only

result.summary: Added a new describe block "REQ-378 §2.2: one-time sync-on-first-login is a one-way gate against post-revocation re-sync" to test/letflow/plugs/iss0736_oidc_live_revocation_test.exs, plus a new test-only OIDC token-verifier double (test/support/iss0736_role_claim_token_verifier_double.ex) needed to reach it. Both existing doubles (TokenVerifierDouble, ConfigurableTokenVerifierDouble) hardcode realm_access.roles to ["VIEWER"], which is not a role Letflow.Api.Authorization.role_allows?/2 recognizes (design §2.3), so neither can prove a synced role actually unlocks a route. The new double claims ["PROCESS_OPERATOR"] instead, activated via a scoped Application.put_env/3 swap (on_exit-restored), same mechanism auth_pipeline_configurable_verifier_test.exs already uses. The new test: binds a PROCESS_OPERATOR tenant_role to a fresh group BEFORE any login (no pre-seeded group_members row); (1) dispatches the brand-new user's first-ever request to GET /api/v1/audit (:AuditRead, granted to PROCESS_OPERATOR) and asserts 200, "PROCESS_OPERATOR" in auth_context.roles, a real group_members row now exists for that user_id, and role_claims_synced_at is stamped (non-nil DateTime) -- proving the sync-on-first-login path fires through the real JIT-provisioning pipeline, not a pre-seeded fixture; (2) calls Identity.remove_group_member/3 to revoke, then re-dispatches the SAME bearer token and asserts 403 -- same live-revocation property as the original AC1 tests, now proven via the real sync path; (3) dispatches the SAME still-role-claiming JWT a THIRD time and asserts still 403, role_claims_synced_at unchanged from the value captured in step (1), and zero group_members rows for that user -- the one-way-gate regression-proof: the sync does not re-fire and silently resurrect the revoked access. Real output, mix test test/letflow/plugs/iss0736_oidc_live_revocation_test.exs --seed 0 --trace: 'Finished in 4.2 seconds (0.00s async, 4.2s sync)' / 'Result: 3 passed' (0 failures) -- all 3 tests in the file pass, including the 2 pre-existing AC1 tests (unmodified) and the 1 new §2.2 test. mix letflow.check.test (the role's mandated warnings-as-errors/ISS-0069 gate) was attempted but ignores per-file args and runs the FULL suite; it failed with 130/211 passed, 81 failures, all attributable to a pre-existing, unrelated branch-state issue (`versions_missing = [20260921000001]`, a migration-state mismatch surfacing in TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 across many unrelated test files) -- not caused by, or related to, the two files this handoff adds. Per an in-session teammate's explicit redirection (this handoff's scope is TEST-RUNNER's full-suite gate to own separately, not TEST-DESIGNER's), this handoff proceeds on the targeted-file run above rather than blocking on that pre-existing full-suite issue. No product code was changed -- test files only.
